title: Valencia and Real Betis Face Off at Mestalla for La Liga
seoTitle: Valencia vs Real Betis at Mestalla – La Liga Preview
subtitle: Teams clash in a delayed first‑round Spanish Championship match on Tuesday.
excerpt: Valencia and Real Betis clash on Tuesday at Mestalla. Get all the details on absences, updates, and likely line‑ups for the encounter.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Valencia and Real Betis will face off on Tuesday, August 25, at the Mestalla Stadium in a match that counts for the first round of the Spanish Championship. The encounter marks the reunion of two teams looking to get their engines going in the national competition after distinct debuts. While the home side tries to score its first league goal, the visitors aim to maintain a 100% win rate.

How the teams arrive for the clash

Valencia comes off a 0‑0 draw with Celta Vigo in the opening round. Although the opponent dominated possession and recorded twice as many touches in the penalty area, Valencia created the best chances but failed to convert them into goals. Real Betis, on the other hand, opened with a 1‑0 victory over Real Sociedad, featuring a beautiful volley from left‑winger Rodrigo Riquelme, after a play that involved the entire attacking trio.

Absences and updates in the squads

Both teams are dealing with physical issues in their squads for the duel. Valencia has up to six possible absences, including right‑winger Diego López, out until January with a knee injury, and rookie defender Justin De Haas, who is likely to miss the game after being substituted at half‑time against Celta Vigo. In Real Betis, midfielder Giovani Lo Celso is unavailable due to a muscle injury, and left‑winger Abdessamad Ezzalzouli remains out with a knee problem. On the other hand, coach Manuel Pellegrini has included the newly signed Troy Parrott, acquired from AZ Alkmaar, and goalkeeper Álvaro de Pablo in the squad list.

Statistics and favoritism projections

Real Betis enters the field with slight favoritism for the match, offering a return of 2.43 on the PrizePicks platform, versus 2.7 for a Valencia win. In last season’s Spanish league, Betis stood out for its offensive power, scoring 59 goals in total, and was the third best away team with 25 goals scored on the road. To try to contain this offensive force, Valencia should adopt a compact tactical formation in a 5‑3‑2 setup.

Probable line‑ups for the match

Coach Carlos Corberán is expected to send out Valencia with Dimitrievski in goal; a defensive line composed of Diakhaby, Pepelu, César Tárrega, Pablo Maffeo, and Jesús Vázquez; midfield with Javi Guerra, G. Rodríguez, and R. Sato; and the attacking pair of A. Danjuma and Hugo Duro. On the Real Betis side, Manuel Pellegrini is likely to start Álvaro Valles; J. Firpo, V. Gómez, Diego Llorente, and Ángel Ortiz; N. Deossa, F. Bernal, Rodrigo Riquelme, Pablo Fornals, and Antony; with C. Hernández in charge of the attack.

With information from BBC, OneFootball, PrizePicks.
